incident_text: Users report that portfolio balances look stale or fail to refresh since about 12:55. Sync errors are spiking.

E-001.claim: aa-sync reports connection pool exhaustion starting 12:56
E-001.excerpt: 2026-03-14T12:56:08Z ERROR aa-sync: connection pool exhausted: 100/99 connections in use, requests queued
E-001.author: reasoning

E-002.claim: portfolio-consumer calls to aa-sync fail with 503, starting before the pool-exhaustion log lines
E-002.excerpt: 2026-03-14T12:51:50Z ERROR portfolio-consumer: aa-sync call failed: HTTP 503
E-002.author: reasoning

E-003.claim: aa-sync pool_in_use jumped from about 22 to 61 at 12:50 and to 100 at 12:55
E-003.author: reasoning

E-004.claim: holdings_snapshot queries in aa-sync begin slowing at 12:50
E-004.excerpt: 2026-03-14T12:50:17Z WARN aa-sync: slow query on holdings_snapshot took 171ms
E-004.author: reasoning

E-005.claim: holdings_snapshot query latency kept climbing to 564ms by 12:55
E-005.excerpt: 2026-03-14T12:55:23Z WARN aa-sync: slow query on holdings_snapshot took 564ms
E-005.author: reasoning

E-006.claim: Postgres latency stayed flat over the window, which contradicts the database being slow
E-006.author: reasoning

E-007.claim: Postgres slow_queries and pool_waiting stayed flat
E-007.author: reasoning

E-008.claim: portfolio-updates queue depth grew to about 1001 while the consumer is the downstream victim
E-008.author: reasoning

E-009.claim: Changes in the window were unrelated: log-level tweaks and a UI copy change
E-009.author: reasoning

E-010.claim: portfolio-consumer depends on aa-sync (caller to callee), so its errors are effects
E-010.author: reasoning

E-011.claim: The slow holdings_snapshot queries are holding connections longer, which drives the pool to saturation. The cause of the slowdown is not identified.
E-011.author: reasoning

H1.statement: aa-sync exhausted its connection pool because holdings_snapshot queries slowed progressively from 12:50, so connections were held longer. This caused HTTP 503s to portfolio-consumer, stale balances and a backlog on portfolio-updates.

H2.statement: An unidentified aa-sync-side problem, such as lock contention, a missing index, a connection leak or growth of the holdings_snapshot table, is the root of the query slowdown. Postgres itself looks healthy.

H3.statement: Postgres is degraded and slowing aa-sync queries.

notes: Why holdings_snapshot queries began slowing at about 12:50 (data growth, lock contention, a missing index or a connection leak).
The aa-sync logs for 12:30-12:50 were not examined beyond WARN level, and no aa-sync config or flag changes were found, so the trigger is unknown.
The 12:51 portfolio-consumer 503s precede the pool-exhausted log lines at 12:56, with pool_in_use already at 61 at 12:50. How aa-sync produced 503s before the pool hit 100 is not explained.
The error logs were truncated at 50 of 208 matches, so the later timeline was not fully reviewed.
